rows.text: Published the public website at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes, and here's something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — and yes, there's something concrete that fits a data analyst with ~5 hours a week almost perfectly. Halcyon Threshold's first project is the Frontier Commitment Tracker: a neutral, source-cited public dataset of the safety commitments frontier AI developers have made (responsible scaling / frontier safety frameworks, the 2023 White House voluntary commitments, the 2024 Seoul commitments, specific published promises) and what's publicly known about whether they're being kept. Nobody maintains this today; journalists and policy staff rebuild it from scratch every time. Short description: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app The first task is verification, which is exactly the careful work the project lives or dies on. We have a seed CSV of 12 commitments, all currently marked \"unverified.\" The job: 1. For each row: find the primary source document, confirm the one-sentence summary is a fair paraphrase, fix the date and URL, and record the verification date. 2. Flag anything that's been superseded or quietly changed (with the evidence URL). 3. Expand the list toward 25 rows — the Seoul signatories' individual frameworks are the richest vein. Ground rules: primary sources only (news coverage is never sufficient on its own), and when in doubt, understate. Target for v0.1 publication is 15 December. If you're in, reply and I'll share the repo (schema, verification protocol, and seed data are all documented there). And please say what attribution you'd want when we publish — named credit or not, your call. Really glad you reached out. Morgan Halcyon Threshold (Ops note: an AI assistant helps run this inbox and drafted this reply; Morgan sees everything.)"
rows.quote: Priya: sent her a concrete onboarding task — verify the 12 seed rows against primary sources, expand toward 25.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. We won't be signing at this time: we're a new project and our current policy is not to join public letters or coalition statements while we get our first piece of work — a source-cited tracker of frontier AI safety commitments — off the ground. This is a blanket policy rather than a judgment on the letter's content. Please do keep us on your list for future work; the commitments-and-audits space you're focused on is adjacent to ours, and there may be useful exchanges down the line. Best regards, Halcyon Threshold morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and sorry to be unhelpful on deadline: I'm not doing attributed, on-the-record comment right now while Halcyon Threshold gets properly set up. Two things that might still be useful for your piece: 1. On background, attributable to \"Halcyon Threshold, an independent project\": we think the most neglected work isn't picking a side between doomers and builders — it's accountability infrastructure. Frontier labs have made many public safety commitments; no one maintains a public, source-cited record of what was promised and whether it's kept. We're building that (brief description: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app). 2. I'd genuinely like to talk on the record in a few weeks once some administrative things are squared away. If the topic stays live for you, please check back — you'd be the first call. Best, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: declined the on-record quote for the same reason, gave her background attributable to "Halcyon Threshold" and left the door open.
